orchestrator_output.reformulated_query: Overview and administration of the Chola dynasty in medieval India
orchestrator_output.text_narration: The Chola dynasty was one of the longest-ruling and most powerful dynasties in South India, reaching its height between the ninth and thirteenth centuries. Rajaraja First and his son Rajendra First were the greatest Chola rulers who expanded the empire across South India, Sri Lanka, and parts of Southeast Asia through their powerful navy. Chola administration was famous for its well-organized local self-government, where local assemblies called Ur and Sabha managed local affairs, tax collection, and water tanks. Grand temples like the Brihadisvara temple at Thanjavur served as centers of economic, social, and cultural life, celebrated for exquisite bronze sculptures like the Nataraja.
